Marginal Derivatives of a Separable Penalty

Source: R/marginal_derivatives.R
penalty_dhessian.DistribPenalty.Rd

The methods of the separable branch for the four generics that a marginal criterion requires beyond the second order. With \(\rho = -\sum_j \log f((D\beta)_j;\theta)\) the Hessian is \(-D'\mathrm{diag}(\ell^{(yy)})D\), so its \(\theta\)-derivatives are the higher components of the parent carried through the same map.

Arguments

pen

A DistribPenalty() object.

beta

A numeric vector of length pen@n_coef. Read by all three derivative methods, because the components of the parent depend on it.

theta

A named list of the free parameters of the parent.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

penalty_dhessian() a list of one base matrix of side pen@n_coef per hyperparameter. penalty_d2hessian() a list of one such matrix per unordered pair, keyed diagonals first. penalty_dcross() a list of one numeric vector of length pen@n_coef per unordered pair. beta_quadratic() a single logical.

The component of the parent behind each method

genericcomponent of the parentresult
penalty_dhessian()distributions7::distrib_cross2_y()\(-D'\mathrm{diag}(\partial^3\ell/\partial y^2\partial\theta_m)D\)
penalty_d2hessian()distributions7::distrib_hess_y_hess()\(-D'\mathrm{diag}(\partial^4\ell/\partial y^2\partial\theta_m\partial\theta_l)D\)
penalty_dcross()distributions7::distrib_grad_y_hess()\(-D'(\partial^3\ell/\partial y\,\partial\theta_m\partial\theta_l)\)

Each component is evaluated at \(D\beta\) and at theta on the parameter scale of the parent, so the derivatives are in \(\theta\) itself and no link is applied.

Nothing is differentiated here. A parent with closed forms for these components, such as the Gaussian and therefore every Gaussian random effect, makes this branch exact. A parent without them takes the fallback of distributions7, which applies one stencil to the highest-order quantity that the family implements itself, usually its analytic response Hessian.

A multivariate parent is read blockwise: each component is assembled into a block-diagonal matrix by dp_blockdiag() and carried through the map by map_quad_full(), and a univariate one goes through map_quad().

Kinked parents

A penalty whose parent declares a kink, which is the lasso and the elastic net, signals an error in penalty_dhessian(), penalty_d2hessian() and penalty_dcross(), with the penalty named (see reject_kinked()). The third derivative does not exist at the kink, and the mode at which a marginal criterion is expanded is where a kinked penalty places coefficients. beta_quadratic() signals no error and returns TRUE for the lasso, whose log-density is linear in the response away from the kink.

The test of beta_quadratic()

The log-density is quadratic in the response exactly when its second derivative in the response does not depend on the response. The generic has already checked theta (an invalid value is an error), and the method evaluates distributions7::distrib_hess_y() of the parent at four points of pen@block coordinates each, and tests with all.equal() at a relative tolerance of 1e-12 whether the values agree across the points. A multivariate parent returns one \(p \times p\) matrix per point, or a single matrix when that matrix does not depend on the response, and the comparison is made between the matrices of different points, not between the entries of one matrix. A single value or a single matrix, which carries no dimension for the points, gives TRUE. If the parent signals an error, or returns a number of values that is not a multiple of pen@block^2, the method returns FALSE.

See also

penalty_dhessian() and its siblings for the generics, distrib_penalty() for the branch, reject_kinked() for the error on a kinked parent, carry_pairs() for the re-keying, penalty_dhessian_beta.DistribPenalty() and penalty_d2hessian_beta.DistribPenalty() for the derivatives of the Hessian in the coefficients.

Examples

b <- c(1, -0.5, 0.3)

# A Gaussian prior at zero: the Hessian is 1/sigma^2 on the diagonal, so
# its derivative in sigma is -2/sigma^3.
g <- distrib_penalty(
  distributions7::fixed(distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), mu = 0),
  n_coef = 3)
diag(penalty_dhessian(g, b, list(sigma = 1.2))$sigma)
#> [1] -1.157407 -1.157407 -1.157407
rep(-2 / 1.2^3, 3)
#> [1] -1.157407 -1.157407 -1.157407

# A Student t prior is not quadratic in the coefficients, so its
# derivative changes with them.
h <- heavy_penalty(n_coef = 3)
beta_quadratic(h, list(sigma = 1, nu = 4))
#> [1] FALSE
diag(penalty_dhessian(h, b, list(sigma = 1, nu = 4))$nu)
#> [1]  0.080000000 -0.004070832 -0.038850928

# A kinked parent has no third derivative, and the call is an error.
try(penalty_dhessian(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3), b, list(lambda = 1)))
#> Error : 'separable [fixed laplace2 [mu=0]]' has a kink, so penalty_dhessian() does not exist there and
#>   its hyperparameters cannot be estimated by a marginal criterion.
